name: KM Robotics WLTR
summary: Industrial robot arm on a linear rail that lays large grooved clay or concrete blocks into walls from a digital plan; co-developed with Wienerberger and built in series by KM Robotics in Czechia.

germany.statusNote: Sold on request by the Czech maker KM Robotics, which shows a net price list and a German-language page and says WLTR is in series production and available at once. No German customer, dealer or service partner is named, and Wienerberger's German website has no WLTR or robot-ready block page. Wienerberger offers WLTR as a bricklaying service through its subsidiary GreenBuild and the joint venture WLTR Masonry Robot, with projects in Czechia, Austria, Slovakia, Poland, Hungary and the UK. The robot needs blocks with licensed grooves.

priceEur.note: Robot hardware only. Software costs €469,000 once or €6 per m² laid (pay-as-you-go). Accessories extra, e.g. transporter €10,900, 2 t pallet truck €2,100, Ford Ranger PHEV as generator €85,000.

germany.leadTime: Series production, 'sofort lieferbar' (maker); no delivery time stated

sellers.name: KM Robotics s.r.o.
sellers.note: Svojšovice 59, 251 63 Strančice, Czechia. Phone line for English; quote form on the page. Price is hardware only; software extra. Offers help with purchase subsidies in most European countries.

notes: Needs blocks with licensed grooves ('Robot Ready' blocks); Wienerberger says 14 such blocks are made in seven European countries.
Builds corners and window and door openings; wall length unlimited (maker).
Runs under the supervision of trained staff and needs careful site preparation and enough room to move (PORR).
Can run without a grid connection from a plug-in hybrid pick-up sold as an accessory.
Figures differ by source: maker 23 m²/h, 90 kg blocks, 5 m walls; PORR 7.5 m²/h (max. 10), bricks up to 52 kg.
How the robot moves between wall positions is not described; armPayloadKg is the heaviest block the maker states.

openQuestions: Is WLTR CE-marked with an EU declaration of conformity? KM Robotics only says 'certified mobile robotics'.
Are grooved robot-ready blocks sold in Germany? Wienerberger names 14 such blocks in seven countries but not which.
Which figures fit the unit sold now: maker 23 m²/h, 90 kg blocks, 5 m walls, or PORR 7.5 m²/h, 52 kg bricks, 3.5 m reach (and 3.25 m walls, 5–7 m²/h in 2024)?
Does KM Robotics deliver, train and service in Germany? No German customer or partner is named.
How the robot moves between wall positions and its footprint; only PORR gives a weight (2,500 kg).
